To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ubiquitin E3 ligase Mdm2 interacts with βArrestin to promote AR ubiquitylation, and that this interaction regulates AR activity in prostate cancer cells.
βArrestins serve as AR corepressors by recruiting the E3 ligase Mdm2 to the AR, thereby promoting ubiquitylation and subsequent proteasomal degradation of AR.
the βArrestin protein βArrestin 2 acts as a scaffold protein for the MDM2 protein, bringing them together to ubiquitylate the androgen receptor (AR), leading to the degradation of the AR.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of βArrestins as corepressors of AR signaling and their potential as therapeutic targets in prostate cancer.
the identification and characterization of novel corepressors of AR signaling in prostate cancer.
the identification of a new AR corepressor that may be exploited for the development of new therapeutic strategies for the treatment of hormone-refractory prostate cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

βArrestins serve as corepressors of androgen receptor (AR), a nuclear receptor that regulates the development and maintenance of male reproductive organs. βArrestins are now recognized as adapter proteins with both cytoplasmic and nuclear target effectors.
βArrestins are bona fide adapters that serve to recruit Mdm2 to the AR complex, thereby promoting AR degradation and the subsequent inhibition of AR signaling.
βArrestins are not only important in regulating G protein coupled receptor signaling, but also play an important role in regulating the activity of AR in androgen-dependent cancer cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
βArrestins are bona fide coregulators of AR signaling and that the expression of β-arrestin 2 is inversely correlated with the activity of AR in prostate cancer.
βArrestins are bona fide corepressors of AR in prostate cancer cells and that the loss of βArrestins in the disease is likely to contribute to AR overactivation.
βArrestins are not only signal transducers but also act as coregulators of nuclear hormone receptor activity in the prostate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
βArrestins are bona fide AR corepressors in prostate cancer.
the ubiquitin ligase Mdm2 is recruited to androgen receptor by βArrestin 2 to facilitate the ubiquitin mediated degradation of androgen receptor.
βArrestins can function in the nucleus as bona fide corepressors of AR signaling.
